Conway.wildlife_intro:
Conway's economy runs on visitors, and its inns, condos, rentals and second homes give wildlife endless quiet shelter. Bats colonize chalet and condo attics in summer, mice and red squirrels overwinter in closed units, and raccoons work dumpsters and decks across North Conway and the village. Conway Lake camps follow the seasonal pattern, while year-round homes get the standard squirrel, skunk and woodchuck mix.

Managers call our crew between guests and owners call at spring opening and fall closing — sealing in fall is the visit that prevents winter tenants. Summer bat discoveries are inspected promptly and excluded after the August 15 restriction lifts. With properties scattered from the village to the lake, Conway work rewards owners who keep one inspection routine across the house, garage and any rental unit on the lot.

faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost in Conway, NH?
faqs.a: Cost depends on the animal, how it got in, and how much sealing or cleanup the home needs, so our crew inspects first and explains the options before any work starts.  Simple single-entry squirrel jobs cost less than full attic exclusion or bat work, and we never quote a firm figure before seeing the structure.

faqs.q: Our North Conway rental smells like mice after winter. What now?
faqs.a: Have it inspected before the next guests arrive. Our crew finds the entry points, checks attic and wall voids for nesting, advises on cleanup, and seals the building. Mouse problems in rentals almost always trace to a few small foundation or utility gaps that a single sealing visit can close for good.

faqs.q: Porcupines damaged our Tamworth barn over winter. How do we prevent a repeat?
